items.title: SAP EWM- Receiving Material in Different Packaging for Same UOM
items.author: Vedant_Gunde
items.text:
Business Scenario: 
 Same material is procured from multiple vendors in different packaging sizes, and it shares the same Unit of Measure (UOM). Because standard system configuration does not allow multiple conversion entries for the same UOM on a single material master, (Eg. 1 CAR = 4 EA and 1 CAR = 6 EA), we need a solution to receive and manage different vendor-specific packaging types for the same material. 
 Configuration: 
 SCM EWM > EWM > Goods Receipt Process > Inbound Delivery >Define Document Types for Inbound Delivery Process 
 Master Data: 
 - Create Product master (/SCWM/MAT1) 

 - Create Packaging Specification (/SCWM/PACKSPEC) 
 2 Packaging specifications are created with Condition type 0IBD is maintained with 2 different Ship from party (Vendor). In level Target quantity is maintained as per packaging supplied by vendor. 
 Vendor 1 supply material in packing of 4 EA in one Carton. 

 Vendor 2 supply material in packing of 6 EA in one Carton. 
 Testing 
 Create Inbound delivery with Supplier 1 
 Delivery replicated to EWM 
 For Supplier 1 from the Packspec (2000066) is determined and hence 12 HUs are created. 
 Create Inbound delivery with Supplier 2 
 Delivery replicated to EWM 
 For Supplier 2 from the Packspec (2000070) is determined and hence 8 HUs are created. 
 Conclusion: Using Packaging specification, condition type > condition record we can receive different packaging for Same UOM.

items.title: How buyers find suppliers on SAP Business Network, and how to show up
items.author: amandalaldin81
items.text:
Every time a buyer runs a search or posts an RFI, the platform checks supplier profiles against the request, whether or not profiles are current and accurate. The same few fields decide who is actually shown to the buyer. 
 That means a profile can look finished and still never appear in search results or RFI matches. The good news is that the fields doing the work are few, and you can change them today. 
 Two ways buyers find you, one set of fields 
 The first is active search : a buyer filters by category, region, or other criteria, and the platform returns a ranked list of matching suppliers. The second is SAP Business Network Discovery matching . A buyer posts an RFI describing what they need, and the platform matches the posting to suppliers whose profiles fit the requirements. 
 Your commodity categories and your ship-to or service locations are the primary fields the platform uses to judge relevance in both. A gap in either one doesn't just limit your search visibility. It can also mean you never get matched to a buyer opportunity you could have won. 
 You can respond to all public sector RFIs and up to three private sector RFIs with no subscription, so better matching pays off right away. 
 Product and commodity categories 
 Search and RFI matching are both category-driven. Categories use UNSPSC, a standard coding system that organizes products and services from broad families down to specific commodities. Buyers don't need to know the codes. They search by keyword, and the platform maps those words to categories behind the scenes. 
 This means that specificity is what gets you matched . If your categories are missing or sit at the broadest level, searches and RFIs in the subcategories you actually serve may pass you by. A supplier of precision-machined components and a general manufacturer don't belong under the same code, and buyers looking for one are rarely looking for the other. 
 Review your categories in the portal and update them to match the products and services you really offer. 
 Ship-to and service locations 
 Buyers often narrow their search results by region, and RFIs specify where the buyer is sourcing from. The ship-to or service location field tells the platform which regions you can serve. 
 Many profiles are still set to "Global" or left blank. This can mean a buyer filtering for a specific region doesn't see you, and an RFI for your region doesn't reach you. 
 Log in to your account , open the profile settings, and compare the listed locations with where you actually do business. If you serve specific regions, list them. 
 Description and showcase content 
 Matching gets a buyer to your profile. What happens next is a different test, whether they arrived through search or clicked through from an RFI match. As Kyle Milan put it in the B2B Exchange series , buyers arrive with zero trust and decide quickly whether to stay. They are scanning for relevance, credibility, and a clear sense of what you do . 
 Think of the profile as a storefront, not a form. A strong description names what you make or provide, the industries you serve, your size or capacity, and what sets you apart. A paragraph about company values rarely does that work. If you have certifications or customer references, keep them current and easy to find. 

 A sample supplier profile as buyers see it, with categories, ship-to locations, showcase files and verification badge in view. 
 Verification 
 Verified suppliers appear 4× as often in buyer search results compared to non-verified suppliers in the same category (SAP internal measurement, 2026). The badge works like a trust signal, similar to a Google Business Profile or LinkedIn verification mark. It appears in search results and on your profile, and tells buyers your business has been confirmed as legitimate before they even click through. 
 Verification is a paid benefit of the promote subscription, and if getting in front of more buyers is the goal, it's worth prioritizing. 
 Small adjustments make a real difference 
 You don't need to rebuild your profile, you just need to close a couple of gaps that have a strong effect on your visibility to potential buyers. If you have 15 minutes today, check two things: 
 Commodity categories are specific to what you sell. 
 Ship-to and service locations match where you actually do business. 
 Each one changes how the platform sees you when a buyer searches or posts an RFI. It's also worth reviewing the rest of the profile from a buyer's perspective and updating anything that's out of date. 
 If you want to take things further, the promote subscription builds on what you already have. It removes the cap on private sector RFI responses and gives you priority placement in search, so the profile work you've done goes further. A Company Showcase section is included too, and promote suppliers appear over 3× more often in buyer search results (SAP internal measurement, 2026). New subscribers can use code DEC26 at checkout for 25% off the first year, valid through December 31, 2026.

items.title: From Specifications to Terraform: My SAP TechEd Takeaways on AI and Platform Automation
items.author: lechnerc77
items.text:
Getting started with Terraform can be a hurdle. You know how you want to set up your SAP BTP account and which services you need, but turning that into your first lines of code takes some work. 

 That was one of the topics I discussed in my interview with Moshe Naveh from the SAP Community team. We talked about my SAP TechEd session, how AI helps with platform automation, and how I use it in my daily work—including making more pull requests for my development team to review. 🙂 

 Click here to watch the whole interview: 

 A bit about me—and Terraform 

 I’m Christian Lechner, a product manager at SAP working in platform automation. I’m responsible for the SAP BTP CLI and our Terraform providers, supporting the administrators who work with SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP). 

 If you’re new to Terraform, the basic idea is straightforward: you define the infrastructure resources you want in code, and Terraform takes care of provisioning them. Instead of setting everything up through clicks in a cockpit, you describe your setup as infrastructure as code. 

 Start with what you need 

 In my SAP TechEd session, we showed a guided approach to generating Terraform code with AI. The starting point is your specifications: your governance requirements, how you want to set up your account, and which services you need. 

 From there, an AI agent, supported by the skills we provide, helps translate those requirements into Terraform code. 

 For me, the biggest benefit is lowering the entry barrier. Getting those first lines of Terraform written becomes much easier when you can begin by describing what you want. 

 Of course, you still need to understand Terraform. That knowledge matters when you work with the generated code. 

 You can explore the project in our GitHub repository: IaC Spec Kit for SAP Business AI Platform . 

 Three takeaways from the handson session 

 The first step gets easier. You can describe your requirements and let the agent help you turn them into an initial Terraform implementation. 

 Spec-driven development is iterative. The name might sound a bit like waterfall, but you can revisit your specifications and go through the flow again whenever you learn something or your requirements change. 

 The right agent skills and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools can speed up development. Giving the agent the right support makes a difference in what you can accomplish. 

 There’s also more we want to do in this area, including support for brownfield scenarios—working with existing setups. That’s further down the road. 

 And of course here is the obligatory selfie after successfully ending the session with all the rock stars that supported during the session: 

 Where I’d recommend starting 

 When Moshe asked how someone new to the topic should get started, my answer had two parts: 

 Learn the Terraform basics. The free SAP Learning course Getting Started with Terraform on SAP BTP guides you through your first steps. It helps you become familiar with the concepts behind the code. 

 Get familiar with your AI tools. Whether you use Codex, Claude, or another tool, explore how to work with it and tailor it to your needs. Understanding the available options is part of getting useful results. 

 Both sides matter: knowing what you want to build and understanding the tools that help you build it. 

 How AI helps in my daily work 

 As a product manager, I use AI as a sparring partner. It helps me reflect on ideas, discuss questions, and explore things I haven’t looked into before. 

 It also helps me write Terraform code for enablement work. I’m not an administrator, so I don’t write Terraform every day. I often know roughly what the code should look like, but I don’t remember the exact syntax. Being able to describe what I need saves me from looking up every statement. 

 And then there are the pull requests. 

 As I joked with Moshe, my development team hates me for this: I can now contribute code more often. Our work is open source and available on GitHub. I can point the AI toward the relevant parts of the code, describe an additional feature, and get help with the tedious tasks. In many cases, the result is already quite decent and needs some fine-tuning. 

 That makes it easier for me to contribute alongside my other responsibilities. 

 Let’s continue the conversation 

 Thanks, Moshe, for the chat and the chance to share what we’re working on! 

 If you want to exchange on Terraform in general, on SAP BTP or using the spec-driven let me know (easiest via LinkedIn). Happy to hear about your feedback and expereinces.

items.title: 从每日重复操作开始：SAP Cloud ERP 中值得关注的 AI 小场景
items.author: Helen_Han
items.text:
查找一组订单、照着邮件改几个字段、整理一段业务进展、弄懂一条报错—— 这类小事每天都在发生。每次多花的几分钟，单看不多，累积起来就占用了本可用于跟进客户、处理业务的时间。 
 SAP Cloud ERP 提供的 AI 辅助功能，可以嵌入到这些具体环节中，帮助你减少重复操作。下面从五个熟悉的场景出发，看看哪些工作值得优先尝试。 
 找信息时，把筛选条件说出来 
 AI-assisted Easy Filter 
 每天打开销售订单列表，你可能都要重复设置几个条件：只看未完成的订单、限定金额范围，再筛出存在交货冻结的记录。这些条件分散在不同字段里，往往还没开始查找，就要先花时间调整筛选器。 
 在支持的 SAP Fiori elements 和 Web Dynpro ABAP 应用中，AI-assisted Easy Filter 让你可以用自然语言表达筛选要求。例如，你可以直接描述想看“未完成、净值超过 3,000 欧元且交货被冻结的销售订单”，系统会把这段话转换成筛选条件，并列出相应记录。你可以逐项检查生成的条件，也可以切回传统筛选方式继续调整。 
 对于需要反复查询同一类业务数据的用户来说，这种方式省去了逐个寻找、逐项设置筛选字段的操作，让注意力更快回到需要跟进的订单上。 

 图：把订单状态、金额和交货冻结要求转换成筛选条件。 
 官方 Demo 入口 
 更新数据时，减少逐个字段的填写 
 AI-assisted Easy Fill 
 客户发来一封邮件，要求调整订单日期和其他业务信息。接下来，你要读懂邮件里的要求，找到对应字段，再把新值一个个填进去。这类操作本身并不复杂，忙起来却容易漏掉其中一项。 
 在支持的 SAP Fiori elements 应用中，AI-assisted Easy Fill 能根据自然语言指令，为多个字段生成填写建议。你可以直接描述要改什么，也可以把邮件里的相关内容粘贴进来；在支持的表格中，还能用指令直接添加行。 
 生成结果后，先核对系统识别了哪些字段、建议的新值是否正确，再按需要修改并确认。例如，把交货日期改为指定日期时，可以对照原值和新值检查，然后再完成应用中的保存操作。业务判断仍由你掌握，重复录入的环节则被简化。 

 图：描述交货日期变更的要求，对照原值和建议的新值后再确认。 
 官方 Demo 入口 
 回复进展时，先生成一份业务摘要 
 AI-assisted Smart Summarization 
 同事问起某张订单的情况，你通常得打开详情、浏览相关信息，再把日期、金额和状态整理成一段话。信息明明都在系统里，重新组织一遍却仍要花时间。 
 AI-assisted Smart Summarization 可为支持的 SAP Fiori elements 对象页面生成摘要。系统默认选中所有字段，你可以取消不需要的，但至少要保留一个。确认后，系统会整理相关内容；你可以在编辑器里调整文字和格式，核对关键信息，再复制到邮件或聊天工具中。 
 在订单跟进、交接和协作中，这相当于先拿到一份可以继续编辑的沟通草稿。需要进一步判断时，仍要回到原始业务数据查看细节。 

 图：把订单信息整理成可编辑的摘要，核对后复制分享。 
 官方 Demo 入口 
 遇到报错时，先看懂问题和处理建议 
 AI-assisted Error Explanation 
 在对象页面上操作时，一旦遇到错误或警告提示，你未必清楚问题出在哪里、该检查什么。尤其是面对不熟悉的业务字段，弄懂报错往往比修改数据本身更费时间。 
 在支持的 SAP Fiori elements 和 Web Dynpro ABAP 应用中，AI-assisted Error Explanation 可以解释错误或警告，并给出处理建议。打开消息弹窗、选中想了解的问题，系统就会给出更详细的说明，帮你判断该检查输入内容、补充资料，还是联系负责的同事。 
 这些建议只是排查的起点，实际修改仍需结合业务数据和权限进行。如需他人协助，可以把解释内容连同具体问题一并转给对方，省去反复说明背景的时间。 

 图：查看错误说明与处理建议，帮助确定下一步该检查什么。 
 官方 Demo 入口 
 准备打印输出时，用自然语言调整本地化表单 
 Form Extension in Localization as a Self-Service 
 日常工作中也少不了收款收据这类打印输出。当表单需要补充信息、调整字段位置或更改纸张方向时，负责模板的关键用户得先把手上的业务要求落实到具体版式中，之后业务人员才能反复使用。 
 Form Extension in Localization as a Self-Service（表单本地化扩展的自助服务功能）借助 Manage Localized Form Templates 应用，辅助扩展本地化表单。你可以用自然语言描述对版式和内容的调整要求，再查看生成的预览。例如，在支持的收据模板中要求添加银行账号字段并将其左对齐，或调整纸张大小和方向。 
 这项能力主要面向负责表单的人员，帮他们准备和维护模板。在确认生成结果之前，需要检查字段是否正确、数据是否对应、版式是否符合业务要求，并在正式投入使用前验证实际输出。适用范围取决于所支持的本地化表单和数据源；模板调整完成后，日常打印即可用上符合需求的表单。

items.title: SAP EWM - Customer Specific HU Picking Using Packaging Specification and BAdI
items.author: Vedant_Gunde
items.text:
Business Scenario: 
 In SAP EWM outbound, when a warehouse task is created, the system picks from the available HUs it finds in stock. One pack size is easy, but what if the same material is stored in different pack sizes and specific customers expect specific ones, in standard SAP system there is no way to pick the right HU for a specific customer. 
 Consider a material, Coke Case, that we receive from two vendors: 
 Vendor 1 sends it in cartons of 4. 
 Vendor 2 sends it in cartons of 6. 
 Note: Below blog can be referred to check, How to receive material in different pack sizes from different vendors 
 SAP EWM- Receiving Material in Different Packaging... - SAP Community 
 On the outbound side, the customers differ: 
 Customer 1 orders it in cartons of 4. 
 Customer 2 orders it in cartons of 6. 
 To handle this, we can maintain the customer's packaging requirement in the Packaging Specification , using outbound condition records (condition type 0OBD) with the ship-to party. The system therefore already knows which packaging belongs to which customer. 
 In standard during warehouse task creation, it does not check which packaging is maintained for the ship-to party of the delivery, so it proposes all the HUs of all pack sizes, and thus customer who ordered packs of 6 can end up with a pack of 4. This leads to wrong shipments, manual corrections in the warehouse, and unhappy customers. 
 In this blog I show how to close this gap. Using the packaging specification condition records and a BAdI, we filter the available quants during warehouse task creation, so that only the HUs matching the customer's packaging are proposed. 
 The Solution: 
 Implement BAdI /SCWM/EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE , method DETERMINE, which lets us filter the available quants before the warehouse task is created and thus can be used to find the right pack size for each customer. 
 Master Data: 
 Create Material Master (/SCWM/MAT1) 
 Create Packaging Specification (/SCWM/PACKSPEC) 
 Customer 1 order material in packing of 4 EA in one Carton. 
 Customer 2 order material in packing of 6 EA in one Carton. 
 Development: 
 Implement BADI /SCWM/EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE. 
 METHOD /scwm/if_ex_core_rms_determine~determine.

 CONSTANTS: lc_lgnum TYPE /scwm/lgnum VALUE 'V001',
 lc_rdoccat TYPE /scdl/dl_doccat VALUE 'PDO',
 lc_cond_typ TYPE kschl VALUE '0OBD',
 lc_stprt TYPE /scdl/dl_party_role VALUE 'STPRT'. "<<< VERIFY type

 TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_hu_ps,
 huident TYPE /scwm/huhdr-huident,
 ps_guid TYPE /scwm/huhdr-ps_guid,
 END OF ty_hu_ps.

 DATA: lv_shipto TYPE /scdl/dl_partyno,
 lr_ps_match TYPE RANGE OF /scwm/de_guid_ps,
 lt_hu_ps TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_hu_ps WITH UNIQUE KEY huident,
 lt_qmat_final LIKE it_qmat,
 lv_ts TYPE timestamp.

 CLEAR: et_qmat_cus, ev_set.

 " 1. Entry checks - only V001 and PDO
 IF is_ltap-lgnum <> lc_lgnum
 OR is_ltap-rdoccat <> lc_rdoccat
 OR it_qmat IS INITIAL.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 2. Ship-to party from the delivery header (query method)
 TRY.
 DATA(lo_dlv) = /scwm/cl_dlv_management_prd=>get_instance( ).

 lo_dlv->query(
 EXPORTING
 it_selection = VALUE #( ( fieldname = /scdl/if_dl_logfname_c=>sc_docid_h
 sign = 'I'
 option = 'EQ'
 low = is_ltap-rdocid ) )
 is_read_options = VALUE #( )
 is_include_data = VALUE #( head_partyloc = abap_true ) "<<< VERIFY flag name
 IMPORTING
 et_headers = DATA(lt_headers) ).
 CATCH /scdl/cx_delivery.
 RETURN.
 ENDTRY.

 LOOP AT lt_headers ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_head>).
 LOOP AT <ls_head>-partyloc ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_party>) "<<< VERIFY component
 WHERE party_role = lc_stprt. "<<< VERIFY field (PARTYTYPE?)
 lv_shipto = <ls_party>-partyno.
 EXIT.
 ENDLOOP.
 IF lv_shipto IS NOT INITIAL.
 EXIT.
 ENDIF.
 ENDLOOP.
 IF lv_shipto IS INITIAL.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 3. 0OBD condition records for this material, valid now
 GET TIME STAMP FIELD lv_ts.
 SELECT ps_guid, pak_ship_to
 FROM /1cn/cpssapobd03
 WHERE kschl = @LC _cond_typ
 AND pak_matid = @IS _ltap-matid
 AND timestamp_from <= @LV _ts
 AND timestamp_to >= @LV _ts
 INTO TABLE @DATA (lt_cond).
 IF sy-subrc <> 0.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 4. Keep packspecs whose ship-to = delivery ship-to
 DATA(lv_shipto_cmp) = |{ lv_shipto ALPHA = IN }|.
 LOOP AT lt_cond ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_cond>).
 IF |{ <ls_cond>-pak_ship_to ALPHA = IN }| = lv_shipto_cmp.
 APPEND VALUE #( sign = 'I' option = 'EQ' low = <ls_cond>-ps_guid ) TO lr_ps_match.
 ENDIF.
 ENDLOOP.
 IF lr_ps_match IS INITIAL.
 RETURN. " no ship-to specific rule -> standard
 ENDIF.

 " 5. Packspec GUID of every HU in IT_QMAT
 DATA(lt_qmat_hu) = it_qmat.
 DELETE lt_qmat_hu WHERE huident IS INITIAL.
 SORT lt_qmat_hu BY huident.
 DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_qmat_hu COMPARING huident.

 IF lt_qmat_hu IS NOT INITIAL.
 SELECT huident, ps_guid
 FROM /scwm/huhdr
 FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT _qmat_hu
 WHERE lgnum = @IS _ltap-lgnum

 " 6. Keep only quants whose HU packspec matches

 ENDIF.

 " 7. Nothing matched -> don't starve the WT
 IF lt_qmat_final IS INITIAL.

 ENDIF.

 et_qmat_cus = lt_qmat_final.
 ev_set = abap_true.

ENDMETHOD. 
 Testing: 
 Create outbound delivery 

 Case 1: Create Pick Warehouse task for delivery. 

 When the warehouse task was created, the system followed FIFO and picked a partial quantity from an already packed HU. This should not happen. We always want to dispatch full cases, in the pack size the customer requires.

 Conclusion: With standard packaging specification data and a BAdI enhancement, EWM can now pick the right pack size for each customer. No change to the picking strategy is needed, and wrong shipments caused by mixed pack sizes are avoided.

items.title: Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition — End-to-End Process Guide
items.author: Angieee
items.text:
1. What Is Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS)? 
 Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) is an automated invoice settlement mechanism in which the supplier does not submit an invoice. Instead, the buyer's system generates and posts the invoice document automatically, based on the confirmed goods receipt and the agreed price in the purchase order. 
 The core principles of this model are: 
 No supplier invoice required — the buyer initiates settlement based on verified GR data and pre-agreed PO pricing. This eliminates invoice discrepancies and manual matching effort. 
 Settlement is GR-driven — once goods are received and confirmed, the system has everything it needs: quantity, price, tax code, and vendor details. No external invoice document is needed. 
 Periodic or on-demand execution — ERS can be triggered immediately after a goods receipt or run as a scheduled batch job at regular intervals, making it ideal for high-frequency procurement. 
 Prerequisite: mutual agreement and accurate master data — ERS only works well when price agreements are clearly reflected in the PO and goods movements are posted promptly and accurately. 
 ERS is especially well-suited for scenarios with stable, long-term supplier relationships and pre-agreed pricing — such as replenishment of trading goods, components, or raw materials from trusted vendors — where the overhead of invoice exchange adds no value. 
 The SAP scope item covering this process is 2LH — Automated Invoice Settlement . 
 2. Business Roles and SAP Fiori Applications 

 Business Role 
 SAP Fiori Application 

 Purchaser (SAP_BR_PURCHASER) 
 Manage Purchase Orders (F0842A) 

 Warehouse Clerk (SAP_BR_WAREHOUSE_CLERK) 
 Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document (F0843) 

 Accounts Payable Accountant (SAP_BR_AP_ACCOUNTANT) 
 Schedule Supplier Invoice Jobs – Advanced (F1683) 
 Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement (MRRL) 
 3. Prerequisites 
 Before the ERS process can run, the following conditions must all be met. If any one is missing, the ERS run will skip the relevant PO line without generating an invoice. 
 3.1 ERS Indicator Set on the Business Partner (Supplier) 
 App: Maintain Business Partner (BP) 
 The ERS indicator must be enabled in the supplier master. Open the business partner with the Supplier business role (FLVN01) , navigate to the Purchasing section, and select the indicator under: 
 Purchasing Data → Additional Purchasing Data → Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) 
 This flag signals that the supplier has agreed to the ERS arrangement — no paper invoice will be issued; the buyer's system settles automatically. 
 3.2 ERS Indicator Set on the Purchase Order Item 
 The ERS indicator must also be set at the individual purchase order item level. The navigation path depends on the app used: 
 Create Purchase Order – Advanced: select the indicator on the Invoice tab of the PO item. 
 Manage Purchase Orders (F0842A): select the indicator on the Process Control tab of the PO item. 
 If the supplier master already carries the ERS flag (see 3.1), this indicator is typically proposed automatically when a new PO is created for that supplier. 
 3.3 Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification Set on the PO Item 
 The Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification (GR-Based IV) indicator must be selected for the PO item. This links the invoice posting to a specific GR document line, which is the foundational mechanism ERS relies on. Without this flag, the ERS run will not generate an invoice for the PO line. 
 3.4 Goods Receipt Must Reference a Purchase Order 
 The goods receipt used as the ERS trigger must be posted against a purchase order (not a free GR or standalone delivery). ERS only processes GR documents that carry a PO reference. 
 3.5 Tax Code Maintained in the PO Item 
 A tax code must be maintained in the purchase order item (e.g., V1 for 19% input tax in Germany). ERS cannot create an invoice document without a valid tax code, as the tax amount must be calculable at the time of automatic posting. 
 3.6 Order Price Must Not Be an Estimated Price 
 The net order price in the PO item must be a confirmed, binding price — not flagged as an estimated price. ERS uses the PO price directly as the invoice price. If the price is marked as estimated, the system will not process the settlement for that line. 
 4. End-to-End Process Walkthrough 
 Step 1: Create Purchase Order 
 App: Manage Purchase Orders (F0842A) 
 Create a standard purchase order against the ERS-enabled supplier. After entering the item, navigate to the Invoice tab of the purchase order item and confirm the following flags are set correctly: 

 Indicator 
 Expected Value 

 Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification 
 ✓ Selected 

 Evaluated Receipt Settlement 
 ✓ Selected 
 The Evaluated Receipt Settlement: Yes indicator is the key control field. It marks this PO line as eligible for ERS — meaning no manual invoice will be received from the supplier; the system will generate it automatically upon GR posting and ERS execution. 
 The Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification flag is equally important. It links the subsequent invoice posting to a specific goods receipt line, which is the foundational mechanism ERS relies on. 
 Step 2: Post Goods Receipt 
 App: Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document (F0843) 
 Enter the purchase order number. The system automatically populates the goods receipt details from the PO. Confirm the delivered quantity and choose Post. 
 The system generates a Material Document (movement type 101). This GR document serves as the trigger for ERS in the next step. 
 Step 3: Execute Evaluated Receipt Settlement 
 This is the core step of the ERS process. Two execution options are available depending on whether you need a scheduled/batch approach or an immediate ad-hoc run. 
 Option A: Scheduled Execution via Application Job 
 App: Schedule Supplier Invoice Jobs – Advanced (F1683) 
 This is the recommended approach for high-volume or periodic settlement scenarios, as the job can be configured to run automatically at regular intervals. 
 3A.1 — Create Application Job 
 Choose Create → the New Job screen opens. 
 3A.2 — Select ERS Job Template 
 In the Template Selection section, select the job template: Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) 
 3A.3 — Configure Scheduling and Parameters 
 In Scheduling Options, check Start Immediately (or configure a recurrence schedule — daily, weekly, etc. — for periodic settlement). 
 3A.4 — Execute the ERS Job and Review Results 
 After the job status changes to Finished, choose Results. The log displays the generated Invoice Document number and the corresponding FI Document number. 
 Option B: Manual Execution via MRRL 
 App: Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement (MRRL) 
 For immediate, ad-hoc settlement — for example, to process a single goods receipt on demand without setting up a job — the AP Accountant can use the Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement (MRRL) app directly. 
 Enter the selection criteria (Company Code, Supplier, Plant, GR document number, etc.) and choose Execute. The system processes all matching GR lines that meet the ERS prerequisites and immediately generates the corresponding invoice documents. 
 This option is functionally equivalent to running the ERS job in Option A, but executes synchronously in the foreground and is better suited for one-off or low-volume scenarios. 
 Regardless of which option is used, the system creates and posts a Logistics Invoice Verification document on behalf of the supplier, based on the GR quantity and the PO price — without any manual invoice input. 
 5. How to Cancel a Supplier Invoice Created by ERS 
 Why Manual Cancellation Does Not Work 
 When a user attempts to cancel an ERS-created invoice directly from the app Supplier Invoices List or Create Supplier Invoice - Advanced (MIRO), the system issues error message: M8414 : "Invoice doc. &1/&2 was created via evaluated receipt settlement." 
 This message is configurable. Via SSCUI 102091 – Define Message Types for Area M8, the message type for M8 414 can be changed from Error to Warning. However, this approach is not recommended. Because even if the message is configured as a warning and the invoice is manually cancelled via Create Supplier Invoice – Advanced (MIRO), the PO line is then no longer eligible for automatic ERS settlement — any subsequent invoice must be posted manually via MIRO. The integrity of the automated settlement flow is permanently broken for that PO line. 
 Correct Cancellation Process 
 The correct approach to cancel an ERS invoice is to reverse the original goods receipt document. When ERS detects a reversed GR, it automatically posts a corresponding cancellation invoice. The process is as follows: 
 Step 5.1 — Enable GR Reversal Despite Existing Invoice 
 By SAP standard, once an invoice document has been posted against a GR, the system does not allow the GR to be reversed. Since ERS creates the invoice automatically after GR posting, this restriction is always present in an ERS scenario. 
 To unlock GR reversal, navigate to SSCUI 106043 – Allow Reversal of GR Despite Invoices and enable the flag: RevGR desp. IR (Reverse GR Despite Invoice Receipt). 
 This configuration change allows the warehouse clerk to cancel the GR even though an invoice has already been posted against it. 
 Step 5.2 — Reverse the Goods Receipt Document 
 App: Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document (F0843) 
 Locate and cancel the original goods receipt material document. The system posts a reversal material document (movement type 102), negating the original GR entry. 
 Step 5.3 — Re-run ERS to Post Cancellation Invoice 
 App: Schedule Supplier Invoice Jobs – Advanced (F1683) 
 Run the ERS job again using the same parameters as in Step 3, referencing the reversed GR document. The system detects the reversal and automatically posts a cancellation invoice (reversal of the original ERS invoice). 
 If the goods are re-delivered afterwards: post a new goods receipt (Step 2) and re-run the ERS job (Step 3). The system will generate a new invoice document based on the pricing conditions valid at that time. 
 6. Full Process Overview 
 Create Purchase Order 
 → ERS flag = Yes | GR-Based IV = Selected 
 ↓ 
 Post Goods Receipt → Material Document (Mvt. Type 101) 
 ↓ 
 Execute ERS Job (Schedule Supplier Invoice Jobs – Advanced) 
 → System automatically generates Invoice + FI Document 
 ─── If Cancellation Is Required ─────────────────────────── 
 Configure SSCUI 106043 → Enable "RevGR desp. IR" 
 ↓ 
 Reverse GR Document (Mvt. Type 102) 
 ↓ 
 Re-run ERS Job → System posts Cancellation Invoice 
 ↓ 
 (If goods re-delivered) Post new GR → Re-run ERS 
 → New Invoice created with current pricing

items.title: Enterprise Search Models in Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608
items.author: siddhant_dutta
items.text:
Introduction — The Challenge of Finding QM Data Quickly 
 Quality Management professionals — whether consultants, quality engineers, or quality technicians — routinely need to locate specific QM objects across a complex landscape of inspection lots, certificate receipts, defects, quality tasks, and master inspection data. Until now, finding these objects required navigating through multiple dedicated SAP Fiori apps, each with its own filter criteria and search capabilities. For a quality technician tracking down a specific certificate receipt during a goods receipt, or a quality engineer searching for open defects linked to a supplier complaint, this multi-app navigation consumed valuable time and introduced unnecessary friction into daily workflows. 
 With the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608.1 release, SAP introduces Enterprise Search Models for Quality Management — a targeted enhancement that brings QM business objects directly into the unified Enterprise Search experience on the SAP Fiori launchpad. This means quality professionals can now find QM objects instantly from the launchpad header bar, without first navigating to a specific app. 
 This blog post provides an advanced, step-by-step guide on what the feature delivers , how to enable it , how to use each search model , and why it matters for your quality operations. A dedicated reference section at the end consolidates all official SAP documentation links for your convenience. 
 1. What Is Enterprise Search in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition? 
 Before diving into the QM-specific enhancements, it is important to understand the broader Enterprise Search framework. 
 Enterprise Search is the central search capability of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. It provides unified, comprehensive, and secure real-time access to enterprise data, enabling users to search for structured data (business objects) and directly access associated applications and actions — all from a single search bar embedded in the SAP Fiori launchpad header ( SAP Help — Enterprise Search Architecture ). 
 Key characteristics of Enterprise Search include: 
 Unified access: A single search bar in the Fiori launchpad shell bar searches across all enabled business objects (purchase orders, materials, cost centers, etc.) and apps. 
 Security-aware results: Search results respect the user's authorization profile — users only see objects they are permitted to access. 
 Relevance-ranked results: Results are ranked by relevance using SAP HANA embedded search technology. 
 Auto-suggestions and wildcards: The search supports auto-suggestions, wildcard matching, and phrase matching for efficient information retrieval. 
 Extensible by key users: Key users can view, activate, and manage SAP-delivered search models, as well as create custom search models from CDS views using the Manage Search Models app. 
 Enterprise Search is included with the base SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition subscription and does not require a separate license ( SAP Discovery Center — Enterprise Search ). 
 Further Reading: 
 Enterprise Search Architecture and Configuration — SAP Help 
 Searching from the SAP Fiori Launchpad — SAP Help 
 SAP Discovery Center — Enterprise Search AI Feature 
 SAP Fiori Design Guidelines — Enterprise Search 
 2. What Are Enterprise Search Models in Quality Management? 
 With the 2608.1 release, SAP delivers predefined Enterprise Search models for the following QM business objects ( What's New in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608.1 — PDF , Section 8.1.1): 
 Search Model Description 
 1 Certificate Receipts Search for quality certificate receipts by plant, material, supplier, purchase order, batch, inspection lot, and more. 
 2 Quality Tasks Search for quality tasks by task code, status, processor, planned end date, defect reference, and follow-up actions. 
 3 Quality Notification Activities Search for quality notification activities by notification type, status, and related attributes. 
 4 Defects Search for defects by detailed description and associated attributes. 
 5 Inspection Methods Search for inspection methods by detailed description. 
 6 Master Inspection Characteristics Search for master inspection characteristics by detailed description. 
 These search models are delivered by SAP as part of the standard product — they do not require custom development. Once activated, they appear as selectable categories in the Enterprise Search dropdown on the Fiori launchpad. 
 What This Means in Practice 
 Previously, to find a specific certificate receipt, a user had to: 
 Navigate to the Manage Certificate Receipts app (F3233). 
 Apply filters manually within the app. 
 Scroll through results to find the target record. 
 Now, with the Enterprise Search model, the user simply: 
 Clicks the search icon in the Fiori launchpad header bar. 
 Selects Certificate Receipts from the dropdown. 
 Types a search term (e.g., material number, supplier name). 
 Navigates directly to the matching record in the Manage Certificate Receipts app. 
 This same pattern applies to all six QM search models listed above. 
 Further Reading: 
 What's New in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608.1 (HFC4) — PDF, Section 8.1.1 
 What's New Viewer — 2608.1 (HFC4) Online 
 Feature Scope Description — SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 
 3. How to Enable Enterprise Search Models for Quality Management 
 Enabling the QM Enterprise Search models involves a combination of feature activation , search model management , and role/catalog assignment . Below is the step-by-step procedure. 
 3.1 Prerequisites 
 Before activating the QM search models, ensure the following: 
 Business Role: The user performing the activation must have a business role that includes the Configuration Expert — Business Process Configuration (SAP_BR_BPC_EXPERT) role template. 
 Business Catalog for Search Model Management: The business catalog SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_ESH_PC must be assigned to the relevant business role. (Note: The older catalog SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_ESH is deprecated.) This catalog provides access to the Manage Search Models app ( SAP Help — Manage Search Models ). 
 QM-Specific Business Catalogs: End users who will consume the search results need the appropriate QM business catalogs assigned to their roles. For example, to search for Certificate Receipts, the user needs the catalog SAP_QM_BC_INCG_QLTY_CERT (QM — Manage Incoming Quality Certificates). 
 3.2 Step-by-Step Activation 
 Step 1: Navigate to Feature Activation 
 Log on to the SAP Fiori launchpad as a Configuration Expert — Business Process Configuration (SAP_BR_BPC_EXPERT). 
 Open the Manage Your Solution app. 
 Navigate to Configure Your Solution . 
 Search for Activate Features and open the configuration activity. 
 Locate the relevant QM Enterprise Search feature(s) and activate them. 
 ( SAP Help — Feature Activation Process ) 
 Step 2: Verify and Manage Search Models 
 Open the Manage Search Models app on the Fiori launchpad. 
 On the Delivered by SAP tab, filter by application area or component to find the QM-related search models (e.g., Certificate Receipts, Quality Tasks). 
 Verify the Activation Status of each model. If a model shows as Inactive , select it and activate it. 
 Optionally, you can edit SAP-delivered search models to customize which fields are displayed and in which order. Save your changes as a draft or publish directly to the catalog. 
 ( SAP Help — Delivered by SAP Search Models ) 
 Step 3: Transport to Production 
 If you are working in a quality (Q) system, the activated and optionally customized search models must be transported to the production system: 
 After saving and activating the search model, navigate to Custom Catalog Extension . 
 Add the catalog and publish the search model to the selection catalog. 
 Use the Export Software Collection and Import Collection apps in Transport Management to move the search model to the production system. 
 The transporting user needs a business role with authorization for these Transport Management apps. 
 ( SAP Help — Transport Search Models ) 
 Step 4: Assign QM Business Catalogs to End-User Roles 
 Ensure that end users who need to search for QM objects have the appropriate QM business catalogs assigned to their business roles. For example: 
 Search Model Required Business Catalog 
 Certificate Receipts SAP_QM_BC_INCG_QLTY_CERT 
 Quality Tasks Relevant QM catalogs for Nonconformance Management or Problem-Solving Processes 
 Quality Notification Activities Relevant QM notification catalogs 
 Defects Relevant Nonconformance Management catalogs 
 Inspection Methods Relevant Quality Planning catalogs 
 Master Inspection Characteristics Relevant Quality Planning catalogs 
 Further Reading: 
 Manage Search Models — Delivered by SAP 
 Creating a Custom Search Model (Video Guide) 
 Transporting Search Models to Production 
 What's New — Feature Activation for 2608.1 (HFC4) 
 Apps for Quality Management (QM) — SAP Help 
 4. Deep Dive: Each QM Search Model in Detail 
 This section provides field-level details for each of the QM search models, including which attributes are searchable, which app the search navigates to, and a practical usage scenario. 
 4.1 Certificate Receipts 
 The Certificate Receipts model is a predefined search for quality certificate receipts — records that document the receipt of quality certificates from suppliers for purchased materials. 
 Searchable Fields: 
 Certificate Receipt number 
 Plant 
 Material 
 Supplier 
 Goods Receipt Posting Date 
 Certificate Type 
 Purchasing Document / Item 
 Batch 
 Inspection Lot 
 Navigates To: Manage Certificate Receipts app (F3233) 
 Practical Scenario: During a goods receipt process, a quality technician needs to verify whether a specific supplier has provided the required quality certificate for a batch of raw material. Instead of opening the Manage Certificate Receipts app and manually filtering, the technician clicks the search icon in the launchpad, selects "Certificate Receipts," types the supplier name or purchase order number, and immediately locates the relevant certificate receipt record. 
 ( SAP Help — Searching for a Certificate Receipt ) 
 4.2 Quality Tasks 
 The Quality Tasks model is a predefined search for quality tasks — activities created in the context of defect processing or problem-solving processes within Nonconformance Management. 
 Searchable Fields: 
 Quality Task and Task Text (note: for technical reasons, internal quality task IDs prefixed with "$" may be displayed) 
 Task Code and Code Text 
 Task Status 
 Processor 
 Planned End Date 
 Defect reference 
 Follow-up Action 
 Related Code Groups 
 Navigates To: Process Quality Tasks app 
 Practical Scenario: A quality engineer is conducting a supplier audit and needs to quickly find all open quality tasks assigned to a specific processor. By selecting "Quality Tasks" in Enterprise Search and entering the processor's name, the engineer gets an instant overview of all relevant tasks — with direct navigation to each task for further processing. 
 ( SAP Help — Searching for Quality Tasks ) 
 4.3 Quality Notification Activities 
 The Quality Notification Activities model provides a predefined search for notification activities — tasks within quality notifications that describe the planning and organizational aspect of notification processing. 
 Searchable Fields: 
 Notification Activity 
 Notification Type 
 Status 
 Related notification attributes 
 Navigates To: Quality notification processing apps 
 Practical Scenario: A quality manager reviewing notification turnaround times can search for specific notification activities by type and status to quickly identify bottlenecks in the complaint resolution process.

 We reinstalled our production SAP Business One server and now the SAP B1 Backup Service is not working. Everything else works fine. 
 Our system:

 - SAP HANA 2.0 SPS08 Rev89.02 (before the reinstall: HANA 2.0 SPS05 Rev59) 
 - SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP5 
 What happens:

 - No backup file is created. 
 - Instead of the normal backup folder, the system creates an empty folder named "PF=".

 From HANA 2.0 SPS08, HANA registers its services on Linux in a new way (SAP Note 3189534). We think our B1 version (FP2408) is older than this change, so the Backup Service cannot read the database name and creates the wrong "PF=" folder. 
 We also noticed that HANA SPS08 for B1 was released only with SAP Business One 10.0 SP 2511 and later. 
 Our questions: 
 1. Has anyone seen this "PF=" folder issue?

items.title: Sustaining a SAP Training Program through a Traditional Education Model in Ghanaian Universities:
items.author: vduah
items.text:
The demand for digital transformation and ERP talent in West Africa is growing rapidly, yet a persistent skills gap limits local enterprise adoption. While SAP University Alliances (SAP UA) and initiatives such as Enterprise Systems Education for Africa (ESEFA) have successfully introduced SAP curricula into African higher education, sustaining these programs beyond initial donor- or vendor-subsidized pilot phases remains a critical challenge. 
 Traditional Ghanaian universities operate under rigid accreditation cycles, constrained IT budgets, high faculty mobility, and exam-driven pedagogical models. Without an adapted institutional model, SAP training risks remaining an isolated extracurricular activity rather than an embedded, self-sustaining pillar of mainstream degree programs. 
 I am currently writing my dissertation which investigates how Ghanaian universities can transition from externally driven SAP pilot initiatives to self-sustaining, curriculum-integrated ERP education models. Specifically, the study aims to: 
 Identify Structural Bottlenecks: Analyze institutional, financial, technical (UCC hosting/connectivity), and pedagogical barriers affecting SAP program continuity in Ghana. 
 Evaluate Stakeholder Dynamics: Examine the interplay between university leadership, faculty champions, students, and local SAP ecosystem partners (employers). 
 Design a Sustainability Framework: Develop a practical operational and financial model for embedding SAP training into traditional university structures without compromising academic standards. And more importantly how to best prepare graduates for the Job Market!. 
 Any suggestions would be highly appreciated.

items.title: Interview with Sindhu Gangadharan: “I Want People to Say ‘That Idea Started in India'”
items.author: Andrea Diederichs
items.text:
SAP Labs India has traveled a long way in 28 years. What began as a satellite operation in the late 1990s is today SAP’s largest R&D hub outside its German headquarters—and increasingly the place where some of the company’s key product work is taking shape. Here, Sindhu Gangadharan, managing director of SAP Labs India and head of Customer Industry Solutions, speaks about customers, innovation, and campus life. 

 When you look at SAP Labs India today, what strikes you most? 
 Photo courtesy of SAP Labs India 

 Gangadharan: You have to go back to understand how far we’ve come. When I joined SAP in the late 1990s, India was seen as an extended workbench, a place where certain parts of work simply got executed. Fast forward to today and that story has completely changed. SAP Labs India is not just SAP’s largest R&D hub outside headquarters; it’s where we define significant parts of product strategy, drive AI innovation, and build technologies that millions of users rely on every day. 

 What also struck me when I returned here after 18 years at headquarters—and this genuinely surprised me—is that SAP Labs India is the only SAP location, including Walldorf, where you have the entire breadth of our product portfolio under one roof. That makes it a natural base for customer co-innovation, especially in an era where working closely with customers isn’t a nice-to-have, it’s a strategic requirement. But if you ask what strikes me most? It’s the talent. At SAP Labs India, we have the privilege of working with some of the brightest minds in the industry, building the next generation of enterprise technology. 

 Can you point to specific products where that contribution is visible? 

 Joule is probably the most prominent example. A significant part of Joule, including the user experience and parts of the underlying engine, was developed here in India. 

 And it’s not a standalone effort. Across areas such as SAP S/4HANA, SAP SuccessFactors, procurement, supply chain, and customer experience, teams in India are helping build AI capabilities that support SAP’s vision for the Autonomous Enterprise. 
 SAP Labs India: where innovation meets impact, and ideas turn into intelligent enterprise solutions for the world 

 Learn more 

 In agentic AI, we are building agents across key business functions, from finance to procurement to supply chain. And SAP Document AI, which won a Hasso Plattner Founders’ Award, had its core innovation rooted here. That product helps remove manual work across hundreds of workflows in hundreds of languages. The team was global, but a significant part of it was sitting right here. 

 What are customers asking for right now? 

 One thing comes up consistently, no matter where in the world I’m having the conversation: they want AI that delivers real outcomes. Not experimentation. Measurable business value. 

 I was recently with the CIO of a large manufacturing company. The conversation wasn’t about piloting AI, it was about predicting equipment failures, improving production planning, and reducing downtime across plants. 

 The other consistent message is about speed. The days of “show me your two-year roadmap” are over. Now that customers are in the cloud, the patience for long transformation programs no longer exists. They want to deploy AI and see value in weeks to months, not years. That is where SAP is very well positioned: by bringing together our business data, process expertise, and application portfolio. 

 You opened the SAP Labs India Innovation Park last year. How important is the new campus? 

 To us, it’s more than an office. The SAP Labs India Innovation Park reflects how SAP is evolving in an AI-first world, where product and engineering teams need to work much more closely with customers. The campus was designed from day one to enable exactly that. 

 Bengaluru is the only location where we have two SAP Experience Centers. You walk in and experience SAP’s AI-powered solutions in the context of real business scenarios: not slides, not demos, but actual working technology. And then there’s the S-Markt, our autonomous, AI-powered retail store. The first is in Walldorf; the second is right here in Bengaluru. When the CEO of IKEA visited with his team, they watched our employees do their daily shopping. He asked me if staff actually use it at scale. Every day, I told him. That’s when it stops being a proof of concept and becomes proof of reality. 

 The location also helps. It is close to customers, partners, Bengaluru’s technology ecosystem, and the airport, making collaboration much easier. And for talent, it creates a very strong sense of purpose: people can work on real customer problems, interact directly with customers, and see the impact of what they build. 

 SAP Labs India Innovation Park at a glance 

 Location: Near Bengaluru International Airport; SAP’s second campus in Bengaluru 

 Scale: Designed to house more than 15,000 professionals, making it one of SAP’s largest campuses worldwide 

 Investment: €194 million across all phases 

 Role: Supports SAP Labs India’s position as SAP’s largest R&D hub outside Germany 

 Focus areas: Enterprise AI, product engineering, customer innovation, and mission-critical services at scale 

 Campus features: Includes SAP Experience Center capabilities and SAP’s autonomous, AI-powered S.Markt, bringing live business scenarios and SAP technology closer to customers and employees 

 What does Indian talent bring that’s distinctive? 

 Look at the structural shift that’s happened across the industry. India today hosts 1,800 global capability centers employing more than two million tech professionals. These centers are increasingly focused on AI, product engineering, and core R&D, not just traditional back-office work. 

 SAP is part of that same evolution. What makes it work? I’d call it a combination of strong engineering depth with a can-do attitude and a genuine hunger to learn. When we ran our Learning Fest on campus recently with a strong AI curriculum and business AI tracks, it was packed. That spirit of wanting to be on top of the latest and greatest, that continuous learning mindset, that’s the secret sauce. Our colleagues are not just writing code; they are taking ownership, leadership, and accountability. That’s a meaningful evolution. 

 Fortune India recently ranked you among the most powerful women “for driving AI-led innovation.” What does that recognition mean to you personally? 

 First of all, I am deeply honored. But I genuinely see it as a reflection of something much bigger than me. It recognizes the incredible work happening at this location, SAP’s long-term commitment to India, and the innovation ecosystem our teams have built together. 

 My name may be on that list, but this recognition is for SAP, for SAP Labs India, and for the remarkable people I have the privilege to work with every day: engineers, product managers, designers, researchers, and customer-facing teams. Innovation is never the work of one individual. 

 Where do you want SAP Labs India to be in 10 years? 

 I would like SAP Labs India to be known not just as a large engineering hub, but as the place where the future of the Autonomous Enterprise was built. For me, impact is not determined by size, but the outcomes we create. 

 My aspiration is that our teams are deeply embedded in SAP’s product strategy—helping define road maps and influence the global innovation agenda. I want that to become the norm, not something we point to as an exception. 

 If, years from now, people look at SAP’s biggest breakthroughs and say, “That idea started at SAP Labs India,” then I think we will have achieved something meaningful.

digest.headline: A thin day: one EWM BAdI case study with unverified code, an SD billing pricing question, and many BTP trial and Joule Studio outage reports.
digest.overview:
The only substantial technical item is an EWM post (15) that filters warehouse task quants through the BAdI /SCWM/EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE, using packaging specification condition type 0OBD per ship-to party. Its code still has VERIFY markers and copy-paste artefacts, and the test results are cut off. The rest is operational noise: BTP trial Integration Suite failures (24, 28), three Joule Studio certification reports (25, 31, 41), an SMS report announcement with no code (9), and a Terraform/AI TechEd recap (10). For ABAP trainers the value is in the EWM BAdI pattern and the two open requirements as discussion cases. The support reports are mainly examples of how to write a bug report.

top_stories.title: EWM: forcing customer-specific HU pack sizes in warehouse task creation via BAdI
top_stories.summary: The post filters candidate quants in /SCWM/IF_EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE~DETERMINE. It reads the ship-to from the delivery header and finds 0OBD packaging specs for that party. It then keeps only quants whose HU packspec matches and returns them in et_qmat_cus with ev_set. If nothing matches, the method returns without setting ev_set, so standard behaviour applies. top_stories.why_it_matters: It is a concrete filter-BAdI pattern built on existing packspec master data instead of custom tables. The fallback decision and the unverified code mean it should be treated as a design sketch, not a working solution.

deep_dives.title: Filter-style BAdI in EWM: steering quant selection with /SCWM/EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE
deep_dives.explanation:
The post implements `/SCWM/IF_EX_CORE_RMS_DETERMINE~DETERMINE` to restrict which quants the warehouse task creation may use. The inputs are `is_ltap` and `it_qmat`. The output is `et_qmat_cus`, flagged with `ev_set`. The logic reads the ship-to party from the outbound delivery via `/SCWM/CL_DLV_MANAGEMENT_PRD=>GET_INSTANCE( )->QUERY` with `is_include_data-head_partyloc`. It then finds packaging specifications under condition type `0OBD`, using `pak_ship_to` and `pak_matid`, with validity checked against a `GET TIME STAMP FIELD` value.

The HU side reads `/SCWM/HUHDR` (`huident`, `ps_guid`) with `FOR ALL ENTRIES` into a sorted table with a unique key. Only quants whose HU packspec matches the customer's spec are returned. Lookups in a sorted table are efficient, but `FOR ALL ENTRIES` needs a guard for an empty driver table. Without it, the select reads everything. It also removes duplicates, which can hide rows if the selected fields are not unique.

The key design point is the fallback. When nothing matches, the method returns without setting `ev_set`, so standard behaviour applies. That means a customer could still receive the wrong pack size, which is the original problem. Decide explicitly whether to fall back to standard selection or to block the task, and log it either way.

Caveats from the post: the code has `VERIFY` markers on party role type, the `head_partyloc` flag and `party_role`, plus artefacts like `@LC _cond_typ` that stop it compiling. It reads the non-standard table `/1CN/CPSSAPOBD03` directly. Packspec content tables are generated and can differ between systems, so a released API is safer where one exists. Treat the post as a sketch.
key_concepts: FOR ALL ENTRIES with empty-table guard
Fallback to standard when ev_set is not set
Avoiding direct reads of generated tables

deep_dives.title: Controlling manual pricing conditions in billing (VF02): where to look
deep_dives.explanation:
The question (S/4HANA 1709, delivery-related billing with VTFL, pricing type G) asks for per-condition-type control: discounts locked, packing charges editable. The post names no mechanism, so the following are control points to check, not a confirmed solution.

The first place is the condition type definition, where the manual-entry setting limits whether a condition can be entered or changed by hand. The second is the pricing procedure, where step control for the condition type can affect changes. Third, the pricing type in VTFL decides how pricing is carried from the order into billing (G in this case), and it applies to the whole item, so it cannot separate discounts from packing charges. The fourth is an enhancement in billing or pricing that rejects changes for named condition types.

Because the requirement is per condition type, configuration alone may not be enough. If one condition type serves both purposes, it may need splitting. Test each option on 1709 before choosing, and check side effects on delivery-related billing, such as re-pricing when the document is saved.
key_concepts: Copy control VTFL pricing type G
Per condition type enhancement as fallback

deep_dives.title: Finding the right standard API: PR to RFQ creation
deep_dives.explanation:
The question (ref 23) reports that the BAPI the user expected does not exist and that no BAdI was found. It does not name what was searched, so the problem is a search method, not a known gap.

A sound order of work is to search the BAPI Explorer by business object for the purchase requisition and RFQ objects, and then check function modules and classes the standard RFQ-from-PR transaction uses. Next, look for purchasing BAdIs in SE18 and SE19 that fit the process. Only if no suitable interface exists should you consider a custom wrapper, and verify what the standard transaction does internally and whether it can be called in the background.

Document type restriction is a filter in your own program: read the PR, select the allowed types, and then create the RFQ. State the release and the PR item types in the question, since availability of interfaces depends on both.

interview_questions.question: You implement a filter-style BAdI that restricts candidate records, and no rule matches. How do you decide the fallback behaviour?
interview_questions.answer: First, find what the business wants when no rule matches: standard behaviour, or a hard stop. In the EWM example (ref 15), an unset ev_set means standard picking applies, so a wrong pack size can still go out. If the rule is a compliance requirement, raise a message or block creation. If it is a preference, fall back and write an application log entry so exceptions can be reviewed. Document the choice and test the no-match case explicitly. Silent fallback hides defects, which is why it should be a conscious decision.

interview_questions.question: What are the risks of FOR ALL ENTRIES in a BAdI that runs during warehouse task creation, and how do you reduce them?
interview_questions.answer: If the driver table is empty, FOR ALL ENTRIES selects all rows without the WHERE condition on it, so guard with an IS NOT INITIAL check. It also removes duplicate rows from the result, so include enough key fields to keep rows distinct. Large driver tables are split into several database statements, which costs time in a performance-sensitive process. Sort or sort-and-dedupe the driver table first. Put results in a sorted or hashed table with a suitable key for lookups. Where possible, use a join or a CDS view instead. Also avoid reading generated tables such as /1CN/ ones directly if a released API exists (ref 15).

interview_questions.question: A user needs to create RFQs from purchase requisitions programmatically and cannot find a BAPI. How do you proceed?
interview_questions.answer: Start by searching the BAPI Explorer by business object for the PR and the RFQ, and check released APIs for your release. Then trace what the standard RFQ-from-PR transaction calls and whether it offers a reusable function module or class. Search purchasing BAdIs in SE18/SE19 for hooks that fit the process. If no suitable interface exists, build a wrapper that reads the PR, filters the allowed document types, and calls the most stable available API. Isolate it behind your own class so it can be replaced when SAP provides a supported API. Document the release, since availability differs between versions (ref 23).
